# Docker Hardened Images to mirror into this repo's GHCR packages.
# Consumed by .github/workflows/mirror-dhi-images.yml and by the drift check in
# .github/workflows/ci.yml.
#
# Each line is a bare `name:tag` relative to dhi.io. The workflow derives both
# ends of the copy from it, so a line can never name a source and a destination
# that disagree:
#
#   dhi.io/<name>:<tag>  ->  ghcr.io/<repo-owner>/dhi/<name>:<tag>
#
# WHY MIRROR AT ALL
# -----------------
# dhi.io refuses anonymous pulls even for the free Apache-2.0 catalog, and the
# third-party charts point the KUBELET straight at the registry — unlike our own
# service images, which are built FROM a DHI base in CI and pushed to GHCR, so
# the cluster never contacts dhi.io for those. Without a mirror every namespace
# running a DHI-based third-party pod needs a dhi.io credential, and the
# monitoring namespace is not even covered by the existing ghcr-pull rotation
# (install.sh passes only common-services/signals/aggregator). Mirroring to a
# PUBLIC GHCR package keeps IMAGES_PUBLIC=true working and leaves the number of
# registry credentials in the cluster at zero.
#
# Licensing: the DHI catalog is Apache-2.0, which explicitly grants
# redistribution (https://www.docker.com/press-release/docker-makes-hardened-images-free-open-and-transparent-for-everyone/).
# The software inside each image keeps its own upstream licence, exactly as it
# does for the Docker Hub bases we already mirror through GHCR today.
#
# ADDING AN IMAGE
# ---------------
# Add the line here AND point the corresponding helm value at
# ghcr.io/blue-dots-economy/dhi/<name>. CI fails if a chart renders a
# .../dhi/<name>:<tag> reference that is not listed here, because that
# combination is an ImagePullBackOff waiting to happen.
#
# Tracking: Blue-Dots-Economy/bluedots-automation#136

# ── helm/common-services — cert-manager ──────────────────────────────────────
# All five are covered by the CI drift check, but acmesolver only just: its pods
# are created by the controller at ACME challenge time, not from a template, so
# it never appears as an `image:` key — it renders as the controller's
# `--acme-http01-solver-image` flag. That is why the check greps the whole
# rendered manifest rather than image keys. If it ever stops being covered, a
# missing acmesolver shows up as a certificate that silently never issues.
cert-manager-controller:1.20.3
cert-manager-webhook:1.20.3
cert-manager-cainjector:1.20.3
cert-manager-acmesolver:1.20.3
cert-manager-startupapicheck:1.20.3

# ── helm/common-services — metrics-server ────────────────────────────────────
metrics-server:0.9-alpine3.23

# ── helm/monitoring — kube-prometheus-stack ──────────────────────────────────
prometheus:3.14.0
alertmanager:0.34.0-alpine3.23
grafana:13.2.0
k8s-sidecar:2.10.1-alpine3.22
node-exporter:1.12.1-alpine3.23
kube-state-metrics:2.20.0
prometheus-operator:0.93.1
kube-webhook-certgen:1.8.5-alpine3.23

# Used TWICE at the same ref: as the prometheus-operator's injected sidecar
# (kube-prometheus-stack) and as alloy's own configReloader sidecar. Listed once
# — the copy is by ref, not by consumer.
prometheus-config-reloader:0.93.1-alpine3.23

# ── helm/monitoring — loki + alloy ───────────────────────────────────────────
loki:3.6.15
alloy:1.18.1

# Grafana's init-chown-data initContainer. Runs as root by design (it chowns the
# PVC for uid 472), so this is not a privilege win — it removes the monitoring
# namespace's last direct docker.io pull. Same tag the aggregator-dpg keycloak
# theme image is built FROM, so it is known good.
busybox:1.38-alpine

# ── helm/common-services — Redis ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# Replaces docker.io/bitnamilegacy/redis:7.2.5, which was BUILT 2024-08-20 and
# sits in a namespace Broadcom froze on 2025-07-18 — it will never be patched
# again, and Redis 7.2 is EOL upstream. That made it the most security-relevant
# image left in the platform.
#
# The `-compat` variant, not the plain one: the Bitnami chart starts the
# container with `/bin/bash -c .../start-master.sh`, which overrides the image's
# ENTRYPOINT, so all the image must supply is bash, cp and redis-server on PATH.
# Plain `redis:7.4.11` has no shell entrypoint at all. Only one tag is mirrored
# here — `7.4.11-debian-compat` resolves to the SAME digest as `7.4.11-compat`
# (verified: identical image id), so there is no second image to copy, only a
# second name for this one.
redis:7.4.11-compat
